name: Elastosis Perforans Serpiginosa

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for Elastosis Perforans Serpiginosa

criteria.description: Presence of characteristic serpiginous or annular keratotic papules or plaques
Histological evidence of transepidermal elimination of abnormal elastic fibers
Dermoscopy showing central keratotic plugs with peripheral erythematous border
Presence of associated connective tissue disorders such as Ehlers-Danlos syndrome or Down syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic clinical lesions plus histopathological confirmation of transepidermal elimination of elastic fibers
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by histopathology; dermoscopy and associated conditions aid but are not mandatory.

laboratory: Histopathology showing transepidermal elimination of abnormal elastic fibers
Special stains (e.g., Verhoeff-Van Gieson) highlighting elastic fiber abnormalities
genetic: Mutations associated with connective tissue disorders in syndromic cases (e.g., Ehlers-Danlos syndrome genes)
other: Dermoscopy revealing central keratotic plugs with peripheral erythematous halo

distinguishingFeatures: Transepidermal elimination of collagen rather than elastic fibers
Lesions often associated with chronic renal failure or diabetes
Histopathology shows elimination of keratin and cellular debris
Lesions are usually smaller and more discrete
Non-inflammatory, asymptomatic papules without transepidermal elimination
Typically affects adolescents with no systemic associations

redFlags: Secondary bacterial infection signs (e.g., purulence, increased pain)
Presence of systemic symptoms suggesting underlying connective tissue disorder
references: James WD, Berger TG, Elston DM. Andrews' Diseases of the Skin: Clinical Dermatology. 13th ed. Elsevier; 2020.
Bolognia JL, Schaffer JV, Cerroni L. Dermatology. 4th ed. Elsevier; 2018.
